name: Terrace of Repose
summary: At the Scarlet Monastery, the Terrace of Repose remains green and clear amid Tirisfal Glades. The Scarlet Crusade tends this courtyard garden, untouched by the Plague of Undeath.

sections.title: An Oasis in the Blight
sections.body: Just north of the Scarlet Monastery's grand entrance, the Terrace of Repose is a green garden amid the blight. Beyond its hedges, grey mist hangs over Tirisfal Glades, where the soil is corrupt and the bogs lie stagnant. Here, a fountain runs with fresh, uncontaminated water, and the Scarlet Crusade tends the garden. Its zealots take these grounds as proof of their divine righteousness and purity. They believe holy devotion can ward off the Scourge's corruption.

faq.q: Why is the grass and water clean here when Tirisfal is dead?
faq.answer: The Plague of Undeath has not reached the Terrace of Repose. The Scarlet Crusade keeps its soil, thriving hedges, and clear water free of the surrounding rot through constant vigilance and perhaps fierce devotion to the Holy Light.

faq.q: Where exactly is the Terrace of Repose located?
faq.answer: The Terrace of Repose lies just outside the Scarlet Monastery's entrance grounds, in the northeastern hills of Tirisfal Glades.

faq.q: What do the Crusaders use the terrace for?
faq.answer: The Crusaders use the terrace as an approach to their fortified monastery and as a quiet sanctuary on uncorrupted earth. They can rest and reflect there, and see an idealized glimpse of Lordaeron as it stood before the Third War.

angles.text: As Forsaken, you see greenery tended by mortal enemies who wish to cleanse Lordaeron of your kind. The living world rejects you, and the terrace is a bitter reminder of that rejection.
As a paladin, you can see living plants and clean water in Tirisfal as proof that the land can heal. Unyielding fanatics tend the grounds now.
